clue.text: Humiliate Pam perhaps, with a wedding song

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the two words are only one possible arrangement of their letters, so they are to be reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone puts Pam down, and a wedding song is involved somehow in the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' tells you to rearrange the twelve letters of HUMILIATE and PAM.
explanation.definitionFit: The classical name for a poem or song celebrating a marriage, sung to the bride and groom.

clue.text: Avenging spirits of old Ireland? Agreed

parts.note: Erin is a poetic, old name for Ireland
yes expresses agreement

explanation.surface: Asking whether vengeful ghosts haunt ancient Ireland, and getting assent.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Irish ghosts; 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek name for the Furies, goddesses of vengeance.

clue.text: " In hugger-mugger 'to him ". (Hamlet)

parts.note: completes King Claudius's words about Polonius in Hamlet, Act 4: 'we have done but greenly in hugger-mugger to ... him'

explanation.surface: A quotation from Hamlet with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Claudius regrets burying Polonius hastily and secretly ('in hugger-mugger'); the missing verb means to bury.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing verb means to bury a body in a grave.

clue.text: They limit the spread of arms

definitions.text: They limit the spread of arms

parts.words: They limit the spread of arms
parts.note: reads like arms-control treaties, but means devices that keep a prisoner's wrists from moving apart

explanation.surface: Treaties that restrict the proliferation of weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' suggests weapons; it means the limbs, held together by restraints.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal cuffs locked on a prisoner's wrists, so the limbs cannot be spread.

clue.text: NO professional turn for the heart specialist

indicators.note: turn asks for the chosen letters to be read backwards
the heart of a word is its central part, here the four letters at its centre

explanation.surface: An amateur takes a turn as a cardiologist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the heart' of SPECIALIST is CIAL; 'turn' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay, not clergy or professional: someone outside the expert class.

clue.text: Don't bother so much with the upper storey vacancy

definitions.meaning: to ... is to care or object to a smaller degree
the upper storey is slang for the head, so a vacancy there means an empty head

explanation.surface: Advice not to fret about an empty room upstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words it means caring less; as one word it means having nothing upstairs, that is, brainless.
explanation.definitionFit: As two words, care less; as one word, stupid or thoughtless, having an empty head.

clue.text: Pope of the City

definitions.meaning: eight popes have taken the name ...
relating to a town or city

explanation.surface: The Pope of Rome, the Eternal City.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of several popes, and an adjective describing towns and cities.

clue.text: Piano, or piece of furniture easy to move

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for soft
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Choosing between a piano or some furniture that is light to shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Light or compact enough to be carried around.

clue.text: Old Bob has conveniently available drink

parts.note: a bob was a pre-decimal shilling, abbreviated S
handy means close by and easy to use

explanation.surface: An old man named Bob keeps a drink within reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Bob' looks like a person; a bob is slang for the old British shilling, written S.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer mixed with lemonade or ginger beer.

clue.text: Purpose of local strain, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is to be judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a strain felt in a particular place could be described as being in tension, written as one run of letters

explanation.surface: A question about the aim behind some regional strain of a plant or virus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks a homophone: 'in tension' (being under local strain) is pronounced the same as the word meaning purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim or plan one has in mind is a synonym for purpose.

clue.text: Little brother has almost all the soup

indicators.note: almost all asks for the word to be shortened, keeping most of its letters but dropping its tail

parts.note: a little brother is still a brother, so this gives the word brother

explanation.surface: A younger sibling greedily takes most of the soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost all' drops the last two letters ER from BROTHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin soup made by simmering meat or vegetables in water.

clue.text: Alas, he was poor !

parts.note: completes Hamlet's famous graveside lament over the skull of the king's jester, 'Alas, poor ...'

explanation.surface: A mournful sigh that someone used to be poor.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests poverty; the clue is the line from Hamlet, Act 5, where the prince holds the jester's skull.
explanation.definitionFit: The dead court jester whose skull Hamlet addresses in the graveyard scene.

clue.text: Piece of wood to point to drifting organisms

parts.note: a plank is a long flat piece of timber
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A carpenter uses a length of timber to indicate tiny creatures drifting in water.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny plants and animals that float with ocean currents rather than swimming.

clue.text: None was worth Landor's

parts.note: completes Walter Savage Landor's line 'I strove with none, for none was worth my ...'

explanation.surface: A remark that nobody measured up to what the poet Landor had.
explanation.walkthrough: Landor's quatrain 'Dying Speech of an Old Philosopher' opens 'I strove with none, for none was worth my strife'; the missing word is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The conflict or struggle the poet says no opponent was worth engaging in.

clue.text: What Tommy got up to!

parts.note: a Tommy is a British private soldier, and the phrase means the sound he was woken by

explanation.surface: Asking what mischief a boy called Tommy has been up to.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy (Tommy Atkins) is the nickname for a British soldier; 'got up to' means rose to, not mischief.
explanation.definitionFit: The bugle call that wakes soldiers in the morning.

clue.text: Concourse for building a machine

definitions.meaning: a concourse is a gathering of people
putting the parts of a machine together

explanation.surface: A gathering called to construct a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of people for a purpose, and also the process of fitting together components.

clue.text: A rise for American liftmen?

parts.note: a lift is an elevator in the US, so the men who run it give people this kind of rise

explanation.surface: A pay rise for lift operators in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' suggests a pay rise; Americans call a lift an elevator, so its operators deal in going up.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising or lifting up, a word built on the American name for a lift.

clue.text: Called together to cook and, vend for a change

indicators.note: for a change says the letters of the preceding words are to be altered in order

explanation.surface: People summoned to prepare food and sell it, as a break from routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' asks for the eight letters of COOK and VEND to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Summoned to assemble, as a formal meeting is convened.

clue.text: Parliamentary vote ? There's the long and the short of it !

definitions.meaning: in the House of Commons, members vote by walking into separate lobbies

definitions.text: There's the long and the short of it
definitions.meaning: school arithmetic has long and short versions of one of its four operations

explanation.surface: A vote in Parliament is the long and short of the whole matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The long and the short of it' looks like the idiom for a summary; it refers to long and short division in arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal Commons vote, where members separate into lobbies, and the arithmetic operation of sharing, done long or short.

clue.text: Has visions, of 240,000 sheets

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500
a ream is a quantity of 480 sheets of paper, and 500 of them make 240,000

explanation.surface: Someone sees visions in an enormous stack of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 240,000 sheets is 500 (D) reams of 480 sheets each.
explanation.definitionFit: Sees images in sleep or imagines things.

clue.text: River divide to the north

parts.note: to sever is to cut apart or divide
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A river splits the land, flowing towards the north.
explanation.walkthrough: The SEVERN is Britain's longest river, flowing through Wales and England.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's longest river, rising in Wales and reaching the Bristol Channel.

clue.text: Stuff that makes Ann uncommonly sharp

indicators.note: uncommonly suggests the letters of the name are arranged in an unusual way

parts.note: keen means sharp, as of a blade

explanation.surface: Some substance that makes a woman called Ann unusually clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncommonly' rearranges ANN to NAN, then KEEN follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff here means fabric: a yellowish cotton cloth originally from Nanjing.

clue.text: Sending out a note with a letter

parts.note: E is a note of the musical scale
a missive is a letter or written message

explanation.surface: Posting a musical note along with a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes something that emits or gives off radiation or light.

clue.text: Ruin associated with brandy ?

definitions.meaning: a brandy ... is a cocktail of brandy, mint and ice

explanation.surface: Brandy brought someone to ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Wreck completely, and a cocktail name, as in brandy smash.

clue.text: Dance is able to be 'repeated

indicators.note: to be repeated asks for the word to be given twice in a row

parts.note: can means is able

explanation.surface: A dance routine good enough to deserve an encore.
explanation.walkthrough: The French high-kicking dance's name is a doubled word.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively high-kicking dance associated with Paris music halls.

clue.text: Sitting on this, one is surrounded by fish

indicators.note: is surrounded by puts the first piece inside the second

parts.note: char is a fish related to trout
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone seated is ringed by fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is surrounded by' places I (one) inside CHAR (the fish).
explanation.definitionFit: A seat with a back, something one sits on.

clue.text: Boss of the horse farm

definitions.meaning: a boss is a raised knob or ... on a surface
a place where horses are kept for breeding

explanation.surface: The manager of a horse farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager; it means a raised ornamental knob.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised decorative knob, and an establishment for breeding horses.

clue.text: Wrongly blame the singer

indicators.note: wrongly suggests the letters are set out in a mistaken order and must be reordered

explanation.surface: Someone unfairly holds a vocalist responsible.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Nellie Melba was a famous Australian operatic soprano.
explanation.definitionFit: Nellie Melba was a celebrated Australian soprano, after whom peach Melba is named.

clue.text: We hear 'little Catherine rouse the bird

indicators.note: we hear signals that the sound of the words matters, not their spelling

parts.note: Kitty is a pet form of Catherine, and to wake is to rouse

explanation.surface: Young Catherine is told to wake up the bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'We hear' marks a homophone: KITTY plus WAKE sounds like the bird's name, though it is spelt with an I.
explanation.definitionFit: A gull of the North Atlantic, named for its call.

clue.text: Greek rose-tree ?.

parts.note: translates the two Greek roots of the shrub's name, the words for rose and for tree

explanation.surface: A rose bush from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: The plant's name comes from Greek rhodon (rose) and dendron (tree).
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen flowering shrub whose name literally means rose tree in Greek.
